title: Maximal complete-permutation spaces with a nonlinear member
summary: Determine whether a maximum-dimensional binary vector space of complete permutations can contain a nonlinear permutation.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist an admissible integer $m$ and an $(m-1)$-dimensional $\mathbb F_2$-vector space $V$ of mappings on $\mathbb F_2^m$ such that every nonzero $\pi\in V$ is a complete permutation and at least one $\pi\in V$ has algebraic degree greater than one? Construct such a space, equivalently a nonquadratic vectorial bent-negabent function $F:\mathbb F_2^{2m}\to\mathbb F_2^{m-1}$ of maximum output dimension, or prove that no such space exists.

scope.domain: Vector spaces of complete permutations and maximum-output vectorial bent-negabent functions
assumptions: $V$ is an $\mathbb F_2$-vector space of dimension $m-1$
Every nonzero member of $V$ is a complete permutation in the source sense
At least one member has algebraic degree greater than one
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later work constructs individual nonlinear complete permutations and smaller vector spaces, but no inspected result constructs an $(m-1)$-dimensional all-complete space with a nonlinear member or proves universal nonexistence.

citations.label: Pasalic--Kudin--Polujan--Pott, vectorial bent-negabent open problems
citations.locator: Open Problem IV.1, Remark IV.2, and conclusion, journal pp. 2710-2712

progress.summary: Open Problem IV.1 asks for an $(m-1)$-dimensional space of complete permutations containing a nonlinear member, equivalently a maximum-output nonquadratic vectorial bent-negabent construction.
